provisioning:Pazar.name: Pazar
provisioning:Pazar.teaser: Shop the stalls against the palace's east wall at eight, while the growers still stand behind them
provisioning:Pazar.story: Treat the Pazar as the galley's vegetable drawer. Walk the whole length once before buying, then go back to the growers rather than the resellers: Kaštela tomatoes, bunches of herbs, honey, dried figs threaded on string, a wedge of Brač sheep's cheese or Pag cheese, a bottle of island oil, slices of Drniš pršut. In late autumn the tomatoes thin out and mandarins and olives take their place.
provisioning:Pazar.why: Go at eight: by noon the best tables are picked over and the growers are packing up.
facts: Kaštela tomatoes, dried figs (smokva), Brač sheep's cheese, Pag cheese, olive oil, honey, herbs, Drniš pršut
About 08:00; the stalls trade roughly 07:00-14:00 (seen May 2026)
Varies by stall and season (seen May 2026)

provisioning:Ribarnica.name: Ribarnica
provisioning:Ribarnica.teaser: Read the morning's catch on the marble before you plan dinner: cuttlefish, red mullet, line-caught bass
provisioning:Ribarnica.story: Let the slabs write the menu. Walk the hall once and see what the boats landed: cuttlefish with their ink sacs intact for a black risotto, red mullet for the grill, line-caught sea bass, gilt-head bream. Ask the seller to clean and scale the fish, and buy for tonight only. The hall's fly-free riddle has its own card in this guide; here the point is to arrive early.
provisioning:Ribarnica.why: Come before ten: the hall shuts around one, and the best fish has gone well before that.
facts: Cuttlefish, red mullet, line-caught sea bass, gilt-head bream
Early morning; the hall closes around 13:00 (seen May 2026)
Priced by the kilo and the morning's catch (seen May 2026)

provisioning:Uje.name: Uje
provisioning:Uje.teaser: A Split olive-oil shop with its own label, and a sister oil bar a few streets away for tasting first
provisioning:Uje.story: Uje is the Dalmatian word for oil, and the shop on Marulićeva sells extra-virgin oils, olive-wood boards and tapenade, with Uje's own oil on the shelf beside bottles from Brač, Hvar and Istria. Taste side by side if you can: the island oils tend to the green and almond-bitter, the Istrian ones rounder, smelling of cut grass. Tastings run at the sister oil bar on Dominisova, an eatery built around oil. A tin or a well-wrapped bottle travels home without trouble.
provisioning:Uje.why: Taste a Brač oil next to an Istrian one before you buy: that comparison is the reason to come.
facts: Shop at Marulićeva 1 (Marka Marulića); the Uje oil bar, with tastings, at Dominisova 3 (Oct 2026 listings)
Check the hours: winter times are not published
Uje's own extra-virgin oil, Dalmatian and Istrian oils, olive-wood boards, tapenade

provisioning:Paški sir and Pag salt.name: Paški sir and Pag salt
provisioning:Paški sir and Pag salt.teaser: Pag's sheep cheese and Pag's sea salt, both shaped by the bura: buy them in Split, three hours south
provisioning:Paški sir and Pag salt.story: Pag is a long bare island of stone and sheep about three hours north of Split by road. When the bura blows from the north-east it throws salt spray across the scrub the sheep graze on, and the old guide hears that salt in the milk. Paški sir, hard-pressed and aged for months, became an EU protected designation of origin in November 2019. The island's salt pans are older still: a will of 999 is cited as the first written record of salt production, and under Venice most of the harvest went to the Republic. Solana Pag is now Croatia's largest sea-salt producer.
provisioning:Paški sir and Pag salt.why: Carry a whole small Paški sir home: it keeps for weeks and grates like an aged pecorino.
facts: Split: the Pazar's cheese stalls; on Pag: the dairies (Sirana Gligora is the name the old guide gives) and the Solana Pag salt works
Dairy and salt-pan visits by booking; check the season
Paški sir PDO, aged six months or longer; Pag sea salt and hand-raked fleur de sel (summer harvest)

provisioning:Stina, Bol.name: Stina, Bol
provisioning:Stina, Bol.teaser: A 1903 co-op wine warehouse on Bol's waterfront, now pouring Pošip, Vugava and Plavac Mali
provisioning:Stina, Bol.story: The tasting room sits in the warehouse of the First Dalmatian Wine Co-operative, built in 1903 right on Bol's harbour front, so close to the sea you hear it while you drink. Stina, founded in 2009, pours the Dalmatian grapes: Pošip, the Vis white Vugava, Plavac Mali and Tribidrag, the grape whose story is told in the history fold. A late-afternoon visit gives a short tour and an unhurried tasting; the room also works as a wine bar.
provisioning:Stina, Bol.why: Buy the Vugava here: it is rarely poured outside Vis and Brač.
facts: Riva 16, Bol, on the island of Brač
Tours and tastings in the season, afternoons; winter opening not published (check before you sail)

walks:Through the palace, gate to gate.name: Through the palace, gate to gate
walks:Through the palace, gate to gate.teaser: Enter by the Golden Gate at half past six and come out on the Riva before the first tour group
walks:Through the palace, gate to gate.story: Start outside the north wall, where Meštrović's giant bishop stands, and pass through the Golden Gate onto the Cardo, the old north-south street, its paving worn to a shine. It opens onto the Peristyle: columns of granite brought from Egypt, early light sliding across them, a sphinx at the foot of the steps. Climb to the round Vestibule, its dome open to the sky, then go down into the great vaulted hall below and out through the small Bronze Gate onto the sea front. Turn right along the Riva to the fishing boats at Matejuška and a glass of Pošip.
walks:Through the palace, gate to gate.why: The Peristyle in empty morning light is the palace as it was built: a stage for one man.
facts: The Golden Gate (Zlatna vrata), north wall of the palace
Short: the palace is about 200 m across; the Riva to Matejuška adds a few hundred metres
About 1 hour 45 minutes with stops, including the Matejuška glass
Polished limestone paving, slippery when wet; steps at the Peristyle and down to the substructures
The substructures' paid wings: about EUR 8 adult, 09:00-17:00 November to March, 08:30-20:00 April to October (Oct 2026 listings; check the City Museum)
Shoes with grip and a few euros for the substructures

walks:Marjan.name: Marjan
walks:Marjan.teaser: Steps from Veli Varoš to a café terrace, then pine paths past hermit chapels to Telegrin at 178 m
walks:Marjan.story: Climb the stone steps out of Veli Varoš and in fifteen minutes you reach Vidilica, the first terrace: a café and a stone bench under Aleppo pines, the palace roofs and the harbour below. Those pines were planted, between 1884 and 1941, on a hill grazed bare. Go on past the Romanesque chapel of St Nicholas, Our Lady of Betlem and St Jerome's, its walls built into the rock face where hermits lived, then up to the summit at Telegrin, with Brač and Hvar across the water. Come back by the south path above the sea to Sustipan, a Venetian-era cemetery turned park.
walks:Marjan.why: Sit on the bench at Vidilica: the whole palace laid out below you explains Split in one glance.
facts: The steps of Prilaz Vladimira Nazora, top of Veli Varoš
A loop over a park of about 340 ha; the full circuit is a few kilometres
About 2 hours for the full loop; 15 minutes to Vidilica, about 45 to the second viewpoint
Stone steps, then paved and gravel forest paths; a stiff climb to Telegrin
Early morning or the last hour of light
St Jerome's chapel under its rock face; the Vidilica terrace (listed 08:00-midnight, Oct 2026 listings)
Water and shoes with grip; a swimsuit if you finish at Kašjuni or Bene

walks:Salona and Klis.name: Salona and Klis
walks:Salona and Klis.teaser: The Roman capital of Dalmatia in the Solin fields, then up to the fortress that guarded the pass
walks:Salona and Klis.story: Before Split there was Salona, capital of Roman Dalmatia, a few kilometres north in what is now Solin. Walk it among olive trees and fig: the oval of the amphitheatre, the ground plan of a 4th-century basilica, the Manastirine cemetery where early Christians were buried. When Avars and Slavs sacked the city in the 7th century, its people fled to the emperor's empty palace by the sea, and Split began. Then drive up to Klis, a fortress strung along a limestone ridge over the pass inland, from whose walls you see Salona, Split and the islands. Game of Thrones filmed Meereen here.
walks:Salona and Klis.why: From the Klis ramparts you see the whole story at once: the ruined city, the palace town, the sea.
facts: Salona is about 5 km north of Split in Solin, about 15 minutes by car or city bus; Klis is a short drive further up the pass
Half a day: about 2 hours for Salona, 1 hour for Klis
The amphitheatre and Manastirine at Salona; the upper ramparts at Klis

Salona EUR 8 adult, EUR 4 reduced, or EUR 10 with the Archaeological Museum in Split, valid 7 days; open 09:00-18:00 October to May (Archaeological Museum, Oct 2026). Klis about EUR 12 adult, hours shorter in winter (late 2025 report; check)

calas:Bačvice.name: Bačvice
calas:Bačvice.teaser: Split's sandy town beach, shallow far out: at six in the morning it belongs to the fishermen
calas:Bačvice.story: Bačvice is a rarity on a coast of pebbles: a shallow bay of sand, ten minutes' walk east of the palace, where you can wade thirty metres out and still stand waist-deep. In summer it is the stage for picigin, which has its own card. Come at six instead. Walk past the changing cabins to the pebble point at the east end, where a fisherman or two may be mending nets. The sun comes up over Mosor, and Hvar turns pale pink across the channel. In late October the sea has cooled to about 18-20°C.
calas:Bačvice.why: The 06:00 hour, when the beach is empty and the light comes off the mountain.
facts: About 10 minutes on foot east from the Riva, past the ferry port
Sunrise; late afternoon in summer to watch the picigin players
A towel and a warm layer: in late October the sea averages about 20°C and is cooling (Oct 2026 averages)
The pebble point at the east end of the bay at dawn

calas:Kašjuni.name: Kašjuni
calas:Kašjuni.teaser: A pebble beach under the cliffs on Marjan's south shore, with no road to the water's edge
calas:Kašjuni.story: Kašjuni lies on Marjan's south shore, west of the Meštrović Gallery, where the pine slopes come down to a long curve of pale pebbles and very clear water. No car reaches the shore, so it stays quieter than the town beaches. In summer there are sunbeds from the beach bar, showers and changing cabins. By late October the bar and the loungers are packed away for the season and the sea is near 20°C and falling. A swim then is short, cold and very clear.
calas:Kašjuni.why: Clearer water than any beach in town, ten minutes by bus from the Riva.
facts: Bus 12 from the west end of the Riva along Marjan's south road, then a short walk down; or on foot from the Marjan paths. Parking is scarce in July and August
Morning, before the summer crowd; in autumn, midday when the sun is on the water
Water shoes for the pebbles, and your own shade and drinks out of season
The view back along Marjan's cliffs from the water

calas:Bene.name: Bene
calas:Bene.teaser: A shaded swim on Marjan's north shore, where the pines reach almost to the rocks
calas:Bene.story: Bene is the beach at the end of the Marjan walk, on the hill's north shore, where the pines grow almost to the waterline and there is shade for most of the day. Behind the rocks are a café-restaurant, showers, tennis courts and a playground, so local families come in summer. It is the place to finish the hill loop with a swim, then take the bus back. In late October the facilities run short hours or close, the water is around 20°C, and you may have the shore to yourself.
calas:Bene.why: The one Split beach with real shade: come on a hot day after the Marjan climb.
facts: Bus 12 from the west end of the Riva to the terminus; or on foot or by bike through Marjan park
Midday in summer, when the shade matters most
Water shoes for the rocks; a picnic out of season, when the café may be shut (check)

around:Brač.name: Brač
around:Brač.teaser: Fifty minutes by car ferry to Supetar, then across the island to Bol and the white spit of Zlatni Rat
around:Brač.story: The car ferry pulls out of Split harbour and fifty minutes later ties up in Supetar, a low town of pale stone on Brač's north shore. From there the road crosses the island's high karst, dry-stone walls and olive terraces, then drops down to Bol on the south coast. Just west of Bol runs Zlatni Rat, a spit of white pebbles reaching into the channel, its tip shifting with wind and current. The island is quarried limestone through and through: the stone's travels and the stonemasons' school at Pučišća have their own cards, as does the Stina cellar on Bol's waterfront.
around:Brač.why: Zlatni Rat seen from the water or the path above, with Hvar across the channel.
facts: Jadrolinija car ferry Split-Supetar, about 50 minutes; the 2026 off-peak timetable (October-December) runs about a dozen daily sailings from early morning to around midnight, fewer on Sundays (Oct 2026). Then about 1 hour by road or bus to Bol

around:Hvar and Vis.name: Hvar and Vis
around:Hvar and Vis.teaser: Greek field walls on Hvar, and Vis, the island closed to outsiders until 1989
around:Hvar and Vis.story: Hvar is the long island south of Brač. Its town has the harbour and the crowds, but the older wonder is inland: the Stari Grad plain, fields laid out by Greek colonists in the 4th century BC and farmed ever since, their stone boundaries still in place, a UNESCO site since 2008. Vis lies further out, the most distant inhabited island off the coast. Yugoslavia kept it as a naval base and closed it to foreigners until 1989; the army only left around 1992. The isolation kept Vis town and Komiža quiet. Eat a viška pogača there and drink a Vugava, both told elsewhere in this guide.
around:Hvar and Vis.why: Vis: an island that missed the tourist decades because the army held it.
facts: Hvar: Jadrolinija car ferry to Stari Grad; catamarans to Hvar town run about twice a day in winter (Oct 2026 listings). Vis: Jadrolinija line 602 sails year-round on a reduced winter timetable from late September. Check every sailing in November
A full day for either; Vis is better with a night
The Stari Grad plain's stone field walls; Komiža harbour on Vis

around:Trogir.name: Trogir
around:Trogir.teaser: A walled medieval town on its own islet, and Master Radovan's carved portal of 1240
around:Trogir.story: Trogir sits on a small island between the mainland and Čiovo, joined to both by bridges. Inside the walls, the lanes are narrower, darker and quieter than Split's. At the centre the Cathedral of St Lawrence keeps its west door, signed by Master Radovan in 1240: Adam and Eve stand on lions, and around the arch run the months of the year, peasants slaughtering pigs and pressing grapes. Venice held the town from 1420 to 1797, and you see it in the Cipiko palace windows and the Kamerlengo fortress on the waterfront. UNESCO listed the whole town in 1997.
around:Trogir.why: Radovan's portal: stand close and read the farming year carved into the stone.
facts: About 30 km west: suburban bus 37 from Split, 30-40 minutes, about EUR 3-4 (Oct 2026 listings), or by car
The Radovan portal (visible free from the square); the cathedral and bell tower, about EUR 5-10, cash only, with shorter hours out of season (Oct 2026 listings; check locally)

around:Omiš and the Cetina.name: Omiš and the Cetina
around:Omiš and the Cetina.teaser: A town wedged in the Cetina gorge, where pirate dukes once charged ships for safe passage
around:Omiš and the Cetina.story: Omiš sits where the Cetina breaks out of a limestone gorge into the sea, the cliffs rising straight behind the rooftops. In the 12th and 13th centuries the Kačić family ruled here and their galleys made the channels to the south dangerous for any ship that had not paid. Their lookout was Mirabella, a 13th-century tower above the old town that watched the Brač channel; the higher fortress of Starigrad, or Fortica, is about an hour's climb. Upriver the canyon narrows into green water and sheer walls, rafted in summer. The klapa festival is the calendar's.
around:Omiš and the Cetina.why: Climb Mirabella: the gorge mouth and the channel the pirates watched, both from one wall.
facts: About 25 minutes by car south-east along the coast road (old guide)
Half a day; a full day with the canyon
Mirabella (Peovica) above the old town; the river road into the Cetina canyon

The Kačić dukes are said to have been expelled after a Venetian defeat in 1287, yet other sources date the end of Omiš piracy to Venetian rule in 1444; Starigrad is credited to the Venetians in the 15th century by some, not all
